title: The One who made the heavens from nothing needs no son.
subtitle: Badi: the Originator with no model to copy

row.title: Badi
sub: made it all with no precedent

then: Mujahid and As-Suddi explained Badi as the One who {idea}brought the heavens and earth into being with no earlier example.{/idea} A child comes from two matching partners, Ibn Kathir notes, and {trap}nothing is like Allah{/trap} to be His partner. He created everything and knows everything.
now: We picture Allah the way we picture people: tired, needing help, needing someone to carry on His name. {idea}The One who made galaxies from nothing has no needs at all.{/idea} That is why you can bring Him every need of yours.
old: I quietly imagine Allah with human limits, like someone who might be too busy for me.
new: He made everything from nothing and needs nothing, so nothing I ask is too much.
try: Ask Allah today for something you thought was too big to ask for.

title: That is your Lord. He made everything, so worship Him.
subtitle: Creator of all, and the Guardian over all
then: After the proofs of seeds, dawn, stars and rain, the verse draws the conclusion. {idea}That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things, so worship Him.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains Wakil as {reward}the Trustee and Watcher who gives provision and protection by day and night.{/reward}
now: Three a.m. and you are lying awake, running through bills, your child's grades, your mother's test results. {trap}You act as if you are holding up the whole sky.{/trap} {reward}There is a Guardian over all things, and He does not sleep.{/reward}
old: If I stop worrying, everything will fall apart.
new: Allah is the Guardian over all things. My job is to worship Him and do my part.
try: Write down your top worry, then say Hasbiyallah wa nimal wakil over it.

title: No eye can grasp Him, yet He sees every eye.
subtitle: The Subtle, the Fully Aware
then: Aishah used this verse to show that no one sees Allah in this life. Ibn Kathir says it does not deny that believers will see Him in the Hereafter, but {idea}no vision can ever encompass Him.{/idea} He, though, {reward}encompasses all vision{/reward}, the Subtle who knows where every thing is.
now: You are alone in your room with your phone. No one can see your screen. {idea}You cannot see Him, but He sees exactly what you see.{/idea} That can feel heavy. It is also a comfort on the nights you cry where no one notices.
old: If no one can see me, it is like it did not happen.
new: He sees every glance and every quiet tear, even when I cannot see Him.
try: The next time you are alone with your phone, pause and remember He sees what you see.

title: The proofs have come. Seeing them is for your own good.
subtitle: Clear insight arrives, and each person chooses to look
then: Ibn Kathir explains Basa'ir as {idea}the proofs in the Quran and the message of the Prophet ﷺ.{/idea} Whoever sees gains for himself. Whoever turns blind {trap}harms only himself{/trap}, for it is the heart that goes blind, not the eyes. The Prophet ﷺ only conveys. He is not their keeper.
now: Your friend sends you a talk that could change how you see your anger. You leave it unopened for weeks. {idea}Nobody can force you to look.{/idea} {trap}Not looking is still a choice{/trap}, and you are the one who carries it.
old: If guidance really mattered, someone would make me listen.
new: The light is already here. Looking or not looking is mine to answer for.
try: Open one reminder you have been saving for later and actually read or watch it today.

title: Explained from every angle, and still they said he copied it.
subtitle: The same verses clarify for some and harden others
then: Allah explains His signs in many ways in this surah, mainly that none deserves worship but Him. Ibn Abbas and others said the deniers responded: {trap}you studied this with people of earlier scripture.{/trap} Yet the same explanations {reward}make things clear for people who know{/reward} and want the truth.
now: Two people hear the same khutbah. One leaves moved and changes something. The other says, "He just read that off some website." {idea}Same words, different hearts.{/idea} You get to pick which listener you are.
old: If something were really true, everyone would see it the same way.
new: Truth can be fully clear and still be refused. The heart decides how it lands.
try: Next time you feel like dismissing a reminder, ask yourself: am I looking for truth or an excuse?

title: Follow what was revealed, and turn away from the mockers.
subtitle: Stick to revelation, and stop chasing every insult
then: In the hardest years in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ is told: {idea}follow what has been revealed to you{/idea}, and turn aside from those who join partners with Allah. Ibn Kathir explains turning aside as {reward}forgiving them, being patient, and enduring their harm{/reward} until Allah brings relief and support.
now: Someone at work mocks your prayer breaks. A cousin keeps sending sarcastic memes. You draft long replies in your head every night. {idea}Keep doing what is right, and let the rest go past you.{/idea} Patience is not losing.
old: If I do not answer every jab, I am letting them win.
new: My job is to keep following the truth. Turning aside can be strength.
try: Delete one reply you were going to send to someone who mocked you. Pray instead.

title: You are not their guard, and not their manager.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ freed from carrying other people's choices
then: The Prophet ﷺ longed for his people to believe. Allah reminds him that {idea}if He had willed, they would not have joined partners{/idea}, and there is wisdom in it. {reward}You are not a watcher over them or in charge of their affairs.{/reward} His only duty was to convey.
now: Your brother stopped praying. Your friend is making choices you hate. You carry it like it is your fault. {idea}You can advise, pray, and love.{/idea} {reward}You were never asked to be their guard.{/reward}
old: If the people I love go wrong, I have failed.
new: I convey with love. Their hearts are in Allah's hands, not mine.
try: Make dua by name for one person you worry about, then hand the worry over to Allah.

title: Do not insult their gods, or they will insult Allah.
subtitle: Giving up a small gain to avoid a bigger harm
then: Ibn Abbas reported the idolaters saying: {trap}stop insulting our gods, or we will insult your Lord.{/trap} Qatadah said Muslims had been insulting the idols and the others hit back by insulting Allah. So {idea}Allah forbade it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir ties it to the hadith about the man who curses his own parents by cursing someone else's.
now: A heated comment thread about religion. You type the cutting line about their beliefs. {trap}The reply will drag the name of Allah through the mud.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the most loyal thing you can do is not post it.{/idea}
old: Mocking what others worship is just standing up for the truth.
new: Insulting their gods only invites insults to Allah. Restraint protects what I love.
try: Before posting about someone else's faith today, ask: what reply will this provoke?

title: They swore they would believe if a miracle came.
subtitle: Demanding signs out of defiance, not to find guidance
then: The idolaters of Makkah swore their strongest oaths: {trap}send us a sign and we will surely believe.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they asked out of defiance, not a wish for guidance. The Prophet ﷺ is told to say {idea}signs are only with Allah{/idea}, and the believers are asked how they can be sure the deniers would believe even then.
now: "If I get this job, I will start praying." "If my test comes back clear, I will change." {trap}You set conditions on Allah.{/trap} {idea}The signs you need are mostly already here.{/idea} The deal is a way to delay.
old: I will commit once Allah gives me a clear sign.
new: Waiting for a sign is often a way of not starting. Start now.
try: Find one if-then promise you made to Allah. Do the then part today, without the if.

title: Refuse the first time, and the heart keeps turning away.
subtitle: Rejection hardens into wandering
then: Ibn Abbas said that when they rejected what Allah sent down, {trap}their hearts no longer settled on anything{/trap} and turned away from every good. Mujahid said it means they were kept from faith, as they refused it the first time. {trap}They are left wandering blindly{/trap} in their misguidance.
now: The first time you skip Fajr, it stings. By the tenth time, you barely notice. {trap}Each no makes the next one easier.{/trap} {idea}Answer the call while it still stings.{/idea}
old: I can keep saying not now, and come back whenever I like.
new: Each time I turn away, my heart turns a little more. The first yes matters.
try: Think of one reminder you keep brushing off. Say yes to it once today, even in a small way.

title: Angels, talking dead, the whole world as witness: still no.
subtitle: Guidance is with Allah, not in the size of the miracle
then: The deniers had asked to see angels, or Allah Himself, face to face. The verse answers: even if {idea}angels came, the dead spoke, and every nation stood up to testify{/idea}, they would not believe unless Allah willed. Ibn Kathir says this is because {reward}guidance is with Allah, not with them.{/reward}
now: You think one more lecture, one more book, one perfect argument will finally fix your doubts or your brother's. {idea}Arguments help, but hearts are opened by Allah.{/idea} Ask Him for it directly.
old: If I just find the perfect argument, belief will follow.
new: Guidance is a gift from Allah. I seek it, and I ask Him for it.
try: Make the dua Allahumma ihdini, O Allah guide me, once with full attention today.

title: Every prophet had enemies who whispered pretty words.
subtitle: Devils of humans and jinn, and their decorated speech
then: Allah comforts the Prophet ﷺ: as you have enemies, {idea}every prophet before you had them too.{/idea} Waraqah bin Nawfal had told him no one ever brought this message without being opposed. Qatadah said there are {trap}devils among jinn and among humans who feed each other polished speech{/trap}. The verse calls for patience and trust in Allah.
now: A video with perfect editing, calm music, and a confident voice tells you everything you believe is a joke. {trap}Polished does not mean true.{/trap} {idea}Notice how good it sounds, and then ask what it is actually saying.{/idea}
old: If it sounds smooth and confident, it is probably right.
new: Decorated words are an old trick. I judge the message, not the packaging.
try: Next time a slick clip shakes you, write its main claim in one plain sentence and check it.

title: Hearts that forget the Hereafter lean into the glitter.
subtitle: Who listens to decorated lies, and why
then: Ibn Abbas explained the word as {trap}inclining toward it.{/trap} The polished words find a home in hearts that do not believe in the Hereafter. They like it, settle into it, and then {trap}do what they do{/trap}. As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said it means: let them do whatever they will do.
now: When you have stopped thinking about the next life for a while, the ads hit harder. The influencer life looks better. The shortcut seems fine. {idea}Thinking about the Hereafter is what keeps the glitter from pulling you in.{/idea}
old: I am smart enough not to be fooled by empty talk.
new: It is the forgetful heart that leans toward lies. Remembering the Hereafter protects me.
try: Spend two minutes today thinking honestly about your own death and what you want to have done.
